answer: Peers re-execute a random sample of each submission, drawn from a rotating pool so no auditor sees the same account twice in a cycle, and a single upheld challenge revokes everything that account earned that epoch. The number that matters is 3, the count of unrelated re-executions required before payment, so a farm of 100 accounts needs 300 independent executions and one whisper of a challenge erases a whole epoch. The anchor is the sample, not the promise, and one plume of copied work is enough to pull it up.
